# `set_batch_stack_setting`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Replace one of the batch-stack input file lists and persist it.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc9dd0, SetFileList @0x3a99c0 (64-bit build) |

Replaces the selected cached batch-stack input list with the supplied file names and writes the list to its persisted file. Refused while a batch stack worker is running. Neither deletes the named media nor starts capture or stacking. Success means the list was replaced; a flush or sync failure during persistence can still accompany a success reply. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0 (the request may also carry key_frame (deepsky, comet) or batch_startrails_mode (startrail), and the comet list has its own persisted file; the 102 rules are on the params schema).

Side effects: Replaces the cached list for the selected batch type and rewrites that type's persisted JSON list file synchronously (flush and sync). Lock and file write may block with no timeout. Partial replacement is not rolled back on a parse or persistence failure. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_batch_stack_setting"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Required top-level object (absent, null, scalar or array gives 107); no positional form. Unknown members are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.type` | string | no | deepsky | Which batch list to replace. Case-sensitive exact match: deepsky (default), startrail or comet. Firmware 9.31: deepsky and comet share one list and persisted file; startrail has its own. Firmware 9.75: each of the three types has its own list and persisted file (the comet list is new). Any other string, or a non-string, gives 102. The 32-bit build ignores this member and always uses the single shared list (firmware 9.31; 9.75 on the 32-bit build shows no list-type strings, string-level only). One of: `deepsky`, `startrail`, `comet`. [READ] |
| `params.key_frame` | string | no | - | Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: optional, for the deepsky and comet types only; a non-string gives 102. The reference frame of the batch (the comet batch uses it as the reference and moves it to the front). If the value is not in the list it is reset to the first entry when the list is stored. Ignored for startrail. Absent in firmware 9.31. [READ] |
| `params.batch_startrails_mode` | integer | no | - | Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0: optional, for the startrail type only; star-trail output mode as startrail_mode (0 maximum video, 1 decay video, 2 both). A non-integer or a value outside 0 to 2 gives 102. Absent in firmware 9.31. Range: >= 0, <= 2. [READ] |
| `params.files` | array<object> | yes | - | Replacement list for the selected batch list. An empty array clears the list successfully. Missing or non-array gives 102. Every element must be an object with a string name; a non-object element, or a missing or non-string name, gives 102. Elements are added in order and the list is cleared before validation, so a late failure leaves a partially replaced list with no rollback. [READ] |
| `params.files[].name` | string | yes | - | File path stored as given. No length, existence, extension or range validation; an empty string is accepted; no storage-root join or traversal normalisation. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent, null, scalar or array | `expected object param` |
| 259 | A batch stack worker is active; checked before parsing | `stack is already running` |
| 102 | Bad type selector (firmware 9.75, an unknown or non-string type; absent means deepsky), a non-string key_frame, a non-integer or out-of-range batch_startrails_mode (firmware 9.75), or files missing, not an array, or an element that is not an object with a string name | `invalid params` |
| 258 | Persisted list file could not be opened for writing | `open file failed` |
| 218 | Short write while persisting the list | `fail to write file` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Failures inside the file write forward the thread-local code; codes originating deeper than the inspected operation are unresolved. Flush or sync failure sets 218 but still returns success.

## Example

Request, set-list - Replace the deep-sky list (shape from the app DTO; values invented):

```json
{"id":41,"method":"set_batch_stack_setting","params":{"type":"deepsky","files":[{"name":"Example/frame_001.fit"},{"name":"Example/frame_002.fit"}]}}
```

Request, clear-list - Clear the default list:

```json
{"id":42,"method":"set_batch_stack_setting","params":{"files":[]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_batch_stack_setting","result":0,"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, worker-active:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_batch_stack_setting","error":"stack is already running","code":259,"id":43}
```
